region 0: lower bound is 0 (no pmpaddr[-1]).\n- Comparison is done on bits [33:2] (word addresses).\n- With PMPGranularity G > 0: mask off the lower G bits of both addresses before comparing.\n\n### NA4 (Natural Aligned 4-byte)\n- Matches a 4-byte naturally aligned region.\n- Region matches if `addr[33:2] == pmpaddr[i][33:2]`\n- (With granularity, NA4 is effectively NAPOT with size 4 bytes)\n\n### NAPOT (Natural Aligned Power-Of-Two)\n- The pmpaddr register encodes the region:\n  - `pmpaddr = base[33:3] | (2^k - 1)` where k is the log2 of half-size\n  - To decode: find the position of the first 0 bit from LSB of pmpaddr[33:2]\n    - If no 0 bit (all ones): very large region — effectively the whole address space\n    - If first 0 is at bit k (0-indexed from LSB of pmpaddr[33:2]):\n      - Region size = 2^(k+3) bytes (or equivalently 2^(k+1) words)\n      - mask = ~((1 << k) - 1) applied to pmpaddr[33:2] bits, then compare with addr[33:2]\n      - Specifically: the upper (32-k) bits of `pmpaddr[33:2]` and `addr[33:2]` must match\n  - Match condition: `(addr[33:2] & mask) == (pmpaddr[33:2] & mask)`\n    where mask has 0s in the low k bits and 1s above\n\n## Granularity (PMPGranularity = G)\n- When G >= 1: TOR and NA4 modes behave differently\n  - NA4 is not encodable when G >= 1 (but the spec says if A=NA4 and G>=1, treat as NAPOT with G+1 trailing Implementation Details\n\n### NAPOT mask computation\nThe pmpaddr for NAPOT has trailing 1s to encode the size:\n- `pmpaddr = aaaa...a0111...1` (k trailing ones)\n- Region base = `pmpaddr & ~((1<<k)-1)` extended to byte address (<<2)\n- Region size = 2^(k+3) bytes\n\nFor matching: `(req_addr[33:2] & napot_mask) == (pmp_addr[33:2] & napot_mask)`\nwhere `napot_mask = ~((1 << k) - 1)` (k is number of trailing ones in pmpaddr[33:2])\n\nIn RTL we can't easily compute this dynamically, but we can use a for loop to build the mask:\n\n```systemverilog\n// Build NAPOT mask: find trailing ones in pmp_addr[33:2]\nlogic [31:0] pmp_word_addr;  // pmpaddr[33:2] = 32 bits\nlogic [31:0] napot_mask;\nlogic        napot_match;\n\n// trailing_ones[k] = 1 if bits[k-1:0] are all 1\n// The mask covers the bits above the first 0\n// Use a priority encoder approach:\n\nalways_comb begin\n  napot_mask = '1; // default: all match (whole address space)\n  for (int k = 0; k < 32; k++) begin\n    if (!pmp_word_addr[k]) begin\n      // First 0 found at bit k\n      napot_mask = {{(32-k){1'b1}}, {k{1'b0}}};\n      break; // Can't use break in SV for synthesis, use different approach\n    end\n  end\nend\n```\n\nActually in SystemVerilog for synthesis, we use a cascaded approach. The real Ibex uses a different approach: they compute the mask using bit manipulation.\n\nThe proper synthesizable approach:\n```systemverilog\n// For NAPOT: mask = ~(pmp_addr | (pmp_addr + 1))\n// Wait, that's not right either.\n\n// Better: use the trailing-ones trick\n// mask[k] = 0 if any bit j <= k in pmpaddr is 0\n// Actually: napot_mask[k] = pmpaddr[0] & pmpaddr[1] & ... & pmpaddr[k-1] \n//           (1 if all bits below k are 1)\n// Then the match region is the bits above all the trailing ones\n```\n\nThe standard approach is to compute a \"mask\" where bit k=0 if we're still in the trailing-ones region:\n\n```systemverilog\nlogic [33:0] pmp_mask;\n// Start with all 1s, then for each bit k from 0:\n// if pmpaddr[k] is 0 and all lower bits were 1, then bit k and above are the mask\n// \n// Simpler: \n// napot_mask = ~(pmpaddr ^ (pmpaddr + 1)) -- the complement of the XOR\n// No wait...\n//\n// pmpaddr + 1 flips all the trailing ones to 0 and sets the first-0 to 1:\n// pmpaddr:   ...a b 0 1 1 1\n// pmpaddr+1: ...a b 1 0 0 0\n// XOR:       ...0 0 1 1 1 1  <- marks the first-0 and all trailing ones\n// ~XOR:      ...1 1 0 0 0 0  <- 1s above, 0s at and below first-0 bit\n// So: napot_mask = ~(pmpaddr ^ (pmpaddr + 1))\n// But we want 1s ABOVE the first-0, not including it:\n// The first-0 position k: we want mask[j] = 1 for j > k, 0 for j <= k\n// ~XOR gives: 1s for j above k+trailing_ones_count... wait\n\n// Let me think again:\n// pmpaddr = ...X 0 1 1 1 (X = \"base\" bits, 0 = first zero, 1s = trailing ones)\n// k = number of trailing ones\n// We want mask = ...1 1 0 0 0 (k+1 zeros, rest ones)\n// Actually we want mask with k+1 zeros at the bottom? No:\n// NAPOT match: upper (32-k) bits of req_addr[33:2] == upper (32-k) bits of pmpaddr[33:2]\n// So mask should have 1s in bits [31:k] and 0s in bits [k-1:0]\n// i.e., mask = {(32-k){1'b1}, k{1'b0}}\n\n// Using the XOR trick:\n// pmpaddr[33:2] | (pmpaddr[33:2] + 1) sets all trailing ones to 1 and the first 0 to 1\n// So: pmpaddr | (pmpaddr+1) = ...X 1 1 1 1 (k+1 ones at bottom)\n// ~(pmpaddr | (pmpaddr+1)) = ...~X 0 0 0 0 -- nope, not what we want\n\n// Correct approach:\n// napot_mask = ~((pmpaddr | (pmpaddr + 1)) ^ (pmpaddr & ~(pmpaddr + 1)))\n// Getting complicated. No...)\n// \n// Actually: napot_mask[k] = ~trail_mask[k] where trail_mask[k] = &pmpaddr[k:0]\n// Wait:\n// trail_mask[k] = 1 means bits [k:0] are all 1, i.e., we haven't found the first-0 yet\n// So if first_zero at position k0:\n//   trail_mask[0..k0-1] = 1\n//   trail_mask[k0] = 0 (because pmpaddr[k0] = 0)\n//   trail_mask[k0+1..] = 0\n// napot_mask = the mask covering bits ABOVE k0:\n//   napot_mask[j] = 0 for j <= k0, 1 for j > k0... \n//   but trail_mask[j] = 0 for j >= k0\n//   So napot_mask = ~trail_mask only works if we shift: napot_mask[j] = trail_mask[j-1]?\n//   trail_mask[-1] = 1 by convention\n\n// I think the cleanest for synthesis is:\n// Compute running AND: all_ones_so_far[k] = AND of pmpaddr[0..k-1] (bits strictly below k)\n//   all_ones_so_far[0] = 1 (vacuously true)\n//   all_ones_so_far[k] = all_ones_so_far[k-1] & pmpaddr[k-1]\n// napot_mask[k] = all_ones_so_far[k] ? 0 : 1... no wait that inverts it.\n// \n// We want mask[k] = 1 iff k > first_zero_pos\n//   first_zero_pos = k0\n//   all_ones_so_far[k0] = 1 (bits 0..k0-1 are all 1)\n//   all_ones_so_far[k0+1] = 0 (because bit k0 is 0)\n//   So: mask[k] = ~all_ones_so_far[k] for the bits that should be 0? \n//   \n//   mask[k0] should be 0. all_ones_so_far[k0] = 1. mask = ~all = 0. MIE=0)\n- On exception: MPP=priv_mode_id_i, MPIE=MIE, MIE=0\n- On MRET: priv_mode=MPP, MIE=MPIE, MPIE=1, MPP=U (or M if no U-mode)\n\n**misa (0x301)**: Read-only = {2'b01, 4'b0, 26'b?}\n- Bit 8=I, bit 12=M (if RV32M), bit 2=C (compressed), bit 4=E (if RV32E)\n\n**mie (0x304)**: Interrupt enable bits for each source\n\n**mtvec (0x305)**: Trap vector base. BASE[31:2] writable; MODE hardwired to 01 (vectored)\n\n**mcountinhibit (0x320)**: Counter inhibit: bit 0=CY, bit 2=IR, bits[MHPMCounterNum+2:3]=MHPM3..N\n\n**mhpmevent3..31 (0x323..0x33F)**: Performance event selectors (writable)\n\n**mscratch (0x340)**: Scratch register\n\n**mepc (0x341)**: Exception PC, bit 0 always 0\n\n**mcause (0x342)**: Interrupt[31] + Cause[4:0]\n\n**mtval (0x343)**: Trap value\n\n**mip (0x344)**: Read-only, reflects irq inputs\n\n**pmpcfg0..3 (0x3A0..0x3A3)**: PMP configuration regs (4 regions per reg)\n\n**pmpaddr0..15 (0x3B0..0x3BF)**: PMP address regs\n\n**mseccfg (0x747)**, **mseccfgh (0x757)**: PMP security config\n\n**tdata1..3 (0x7A1..0x7A3)**, **tselect (0x7A0)**: Debug trigger (if DbgTriggerEn)\n\n**dcsr (0x7B0)**, **dpc (0x7B1)**, **dscratch0,1 (0x7B2,3)**: Debug CSRs\n\n**cpuctrlsts (0x7C0)**: Custom: bits [0]=icache_en, [1]=data_ind_timing, [2]=dummy_instr_en, [5:3]=dummy_instr_mask, [6]=sync_exc_seen, [7]=double_fault_seen, [8]=ic_scr_key_valid\n\n**secureseed (0x7C1)**: Write-only LFSR seed\n\n**mcycle (0xB00)**, **mcycleh (0xB80)**: Cycle counter\n**minstret (0xB02)**, **minstreth (0xB82)**: Instruction retire counter\n**mhpmcounter3..31 (0xB03..0xB1F)**: HPM counters\n**mhpmcounter3h..31h (0xB83..0xB9F)**: HPM counter high halves\n\n**mhartid (0xF14)**: Read-only = hart_id_i\n**mvendorid (0xF11)**: Read-only = 0\n**marchid (0xF12)**: Read-only = 32'h16\n**mimpid (0xF13)**: Read-only = 0\n\n### Counter implementation:\nUse `ibex_counter` instances for mcycle/minstret/mhpmcounters. Connect increment signals.\n\n### The CSR read mux:\nIn a big `always_comb` or `unique case` on `csr_addr_i`, set `csr_rdata_o`.\n\n### The CSR write operation:\nUse ibex_csr instances for key registers (mstatus, mie, etc.) with shadow copy for SecureIbex.\nOr implement directly with always_ff blocks.\n\n### Illegal CSR detection:\n`illegal_csr_insn_o` = 1 when:\n- CSR address is not implemented\n- Access type requires write but CSR is read-only\n- Debug-mode-only CSRs accessed outside debug mode\n- PMP CSRs accessed when PMPEnable=0 (still implemented but WARL)\n\n## IMPORTANT Implementation Notes\n\n1. The test exercises: reading/writing standard CSRs, illegal CSR detection, PMP CSRs\n4. Performance counter test: reads mcycle, writes mcountinhibit\n5. Use ibex_counter for cycle/instret counters. After inhibiting mcycle, should it stop? The C++ model ignores mcycle mismatches so we don't need to worry about timing.\n\nFor simplicity, let's implement:\n- mcycle: 64-bit counter, always increments unless mcountinhibit[0]=1\n- minstret: 64-bit counter, increments on instr_ret_i unless mcountinhibit[2]=1\n- mhpmcounters: stay at written value (no increment since no event sources connected in test)\n\nActually since event connections (instr_ret_i etc.) are all unconnected (0), no incrementing will happen for minstret either. And mcycle will always increment since clk is always running.\n\nFor the test: mcycle read value grows but the C++ model ignores it. So we just need the write-back to work correctly.\n\n### mhpmevent reset value behavior\n\nFor mhpmevent[i] (i=3..MHPMCounterNum+2): reset to 1<<(i-3), all bits locked (read-only from C++ perspective). In RTL: implement as reset-only registers, writes have no effect... \n\nActually that means they ARE writable registers but writes get ignored because lock_mask=all-1. Hmm.\n\nWait, if lock_mask=0xFFFFFFFF:\n```\nregister_value_ &= lock_mask;  // = register_value_ (all bits kept)\nregister_value_ |= (newval & 0); // = 0\n// result = register_value_ unchanged\n```\nSo yes, they're effectively read-only in the model. Our RTL should just return the reset value and ignore writes.\n\n### Final approach for mhpmevent\n\nLooking more carefully: mhpmevent in real ibex IS writable. But the C++ model has them as \"WARL with mask=0xFFFFFFFF\" which means read-only. This is the test's model.\n\nFor the RTL to pass: we need mhpmevent reads to return the reset value (1<<(i-3)) after reset, and writes to have no effect.\n\nWait, but actually if writes have no effect and we always return reset value, that's easy. We just hardwire the value.\n\nBUT: that seems wrong for real hardware. Let me look at what happens:\n\nThe test does random writes to mhpmevent3. After writing, it reads back. The C++ model expects read_value = 1 (the reset value, since writes don't change it). So our RTL must also return 1 always for mhpmevent3. This means the RTL mhpmevent registers should be read-only constants at their reset values.\n\nOK this is fine. We implement them as constants (or registers that don't update on write).\n\n### mhpmcounter behavior\n\nFor mhpmcounters (implemented): mask for lock changes with MHPMCounterWidth.\n- Low 32 bits: lock = ~((1<<MHPMCounterWidth)-1) & 0xFFFFFFFF\n  - For width=40: lock = 0x0 (all writable)\n  - For width=32: lock = 0x0 (all writable) \n  - For width=64: lock = 0x0 (all writable, since 64-bit mask is all 0s)\n- High bits: lock = (~((1<<MHPMCounterWidth)-1)) >> 32\n  - For width=40: lock = 0xFFFFFF00 (upper 24 locked at 0)\n  - For width=32: lock = 0xFFFFFFFF (all high bits locked at 0)\n  - For width=64: lock = 0x00000000 (all writable)\n\nThe counter value also increments if counting, but since event sources are 0 in the test, no increment happens.\n\nFor MCycle (BaseRegister): fully read/write 32-bit. BUT mcycle actually increments. Since C++ model ignores mcycle reads, we can safely increment it.\n\n### PMP register behavior\n\nFor PMPCfg:\n- When PMPEnable=0: all 4 pmpcfg regs are NonImp (return 0, not illegal)\n- When PMPEnable=1: pmpcfg[i] implemented if i < ceil(PMPNumRegions/4)\n- Lock bits prevent modification (unless RLB set in mseccfg)\n- Reserved W=1,R=0 patterns cleared (unless MML set)\n- Bits [6:5] of each byte are always 0 (raz_mask_ = 0x9F9F9F9F clears bits [6:5])\n\nFor PMPAddr:\n- When PMPEnable=0: all NonImp (return 0, not illegal)\n- When PMPEnable=1: pmpaddr[i] implemented if i < PMPNumRegions\n- Locked if cfg.lock set OR next region uses TOR mode\n- Returns addr[31:0] (the 32-bit portion stored)\n\n## Detailed RTL Structure\n\n### CSR read mux\n```systemverilog\nalways_comb begin\n  csr_rdata_o = '0;\n  illegal_csr_insn_o = csr_access_i;  // assume illegal, clear below\n  \n  if (csr_access_i) begin\n    unique case (csr_addr_i)\n      CSR_MSTATUS: begin\n        csr_rdata_o = mstatus_rdata;\n        illegal_csr_insn_o = 1'b0;\n      end\n      // ... all implemented CSRs\n      default: begin\n        csr_rdata_o = '0;\n        illegal_csr_insn_o = 1'b1;\n      end\n    endcase\n  end\nend\n```\n\n### CSR write logic\nFor each writable CSR, compute write enable and write data based on op:\n```\nwr_en = csr_access_i & csr_op_en_i & !illegal_csr_insn_o & (csr_op_i != CSR_OP_READ)\n```\n\nThe write data depends on op:\n- WRITE: csr_wdata_i\n- SET:   current_val | csr_wdata_i\n- CLEAR: current_val & ~csr_wdata_i\n- READ:  (no write)\n\n### Register storage\n\nUse plain always_ff for all registers. For PMPCfg, apply masks on write.\n\n## Full List of Implemented CSRs (return 0 but NOT illegal)\n\nFrom the C++ model (csr_listing.def), ALL of these must NOT be illegal:\n- PMPCfg0-3, PMPAddr0-15 (even when PMPEnable=0 → return 0)\n- MCountInhibit\n- MHPMEvent3-31 (even unimplemented ones → return 0)\n- MSeccfg, MSeccfgh\n- MCycle, MCycleH\n- MInstret, MInstretH\n- MHPMCounter3-31, MHPMCounter3H-31H (even unimplemented → return 0)\n\nWait: for non-implemented mhpmevent (i > MHPMCounterNum+2): model uses NonImpRegister which reads as 0 and is NOT illegal (it matches address).
